vocabulary.meaning_en: words you say when you meet someone
vocabulary.example: "Good morning" is a polite greeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: relaxed and friendly, not formal
vocabulary.example: "Hey!" is a casual greeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: polite and serious, for work or new people
vocabulary.example: Use formal English with your manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a lot to do
vocabulary.example: I'm busy with school this week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: rest and feel calm
vocabulary.example: I want to relax today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small place where you buy and drink coffee
vocabulary.example: Let's meet at the coffee shop.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you choose
vocabulary.example: Tea is a good choice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: Saturday and Sunday, or the days off work
vocabulary.example: What are your plans for the weekend?

vocabulary.meaning_en: talk with someone about what happened since you last met
vocabulary.example: It's nice to catch up with old friends.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an animal that lives with you at home
vocabulary.example: Do you have a pet?

vocabulary.meaning_en: kind and nice to people
vocabulary.example: Our neighbor is very friendly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: liking to play
vocabulary.example: The kitten is very playful.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a happy feeling
vocabulary.example: It's a pleasure to meet you.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a big formal meeting with talks
vocabulary.example: She is speaking at a conference.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who gives a talk
vocabulary.example: The first speaker was very good.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a talk that explains something to a group
vocabulary.example: He gave a presentation about his project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: your job or position in a group
vocabulary.example: What is your role in the team?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a manager of a company department
vocabulary.example: She is the sales director.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who buys services from a company
vocabulary.example: We have a meeting with a new client.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small card with your name, job and phone number
vocabulary.example: Here is my business card.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list of things to talk about in a meeting
vocabulary.example: The first item on the agenda is the budget.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an idea about what to do
vocabulary.example: I have a suggestion for the project.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the money you can spend on something
vocabulary.example: We need to plan the budget carefully.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a plan that shows when things will happen
vocabulary.example: The timeline for the project is three months.

fine_lines.title: Casual vs formal greetings
fine_lines.explanation_ar: مع الأصدقاء نستخدم تحيات غير رسمية: Hey! / Good to see you! / How have you been? ومع الأشخاص في العمل أو الغرباء نستخدم تحيات رسمية: Good morning, Mr Smith. / It is a pleasure to meet you.
fine_lines.explanation_en: With friends: Hey! / Good to see you! With work people: Good morning, Mr Smith. / It is a pleasure to meet you.

examples.sentence: Hey, Mia! Good to see you!

fine_lines.title: Mr vs Ms
fine_lines.explanation_ar: في المواقف الرسمية نضع Mr قبل اسم عائلة الرجل، و Ms قبل اسم عائلة المرأة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: In formal situations: Mr + a man's family name, Ms + a woman's family name.

fine_lines.title: Good morning vs Good afternoon
fine_lines.explanation_ar: Good morning من الصباح حتى الظهر، و Good afternoon من الظهر حتى المساء تقريبًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Good morning is for before 12 o'clock. Good afternoon is for after 12 until the evening.

examples.sentence: Good afternoon. How are you today?

expressions.phrase: Good to see you! / You too!
expressions.meaning_en: A casual greeting for a friend.
expressions.example: Hey, Jake! Good to see you! You too!

expressions.phrase: How have you been? — I've been good, thanks!
expressions.meaning_ar: كيف كانت أحوالك؟ — كنت بخير، شكرًا!
expressions.meaning_en: Ask a friend about the time since you last met.
expressions.example: How have you been? I've been good, thanks. Just busy.

expressions.meaning_en: Casual: the same is true for me.

expressions.phrase: What can I get for you today?
expressions.meaning_en: What a waiter or shop worker says.
expressions.example: Hello! What can I get for you today?

expressions.meaning_en: Say you enjoyed talking with an old friend.
expressions.example: It was nice to catch up, Mia!

expressions.phrase: It is a pleasure to meet you. — The pleasure is mine.
expressions.meaning_en: A formal greeting and its reply.
expressions.example: It is a pleasure to meet you, Mr Smith. The pleasure is mine.

expressions.phrase: I am doing well, thank you for asking.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite, formal answer to "How are you?".
expressions.example: How are you, Ms Lee? I am doing well, thank you for asking.

expressions.meaning_en: Formal: say you are waiting happily for something.
expressions.example: I look forward to your message.

expressions.phrase: Would you like to exchange business cards?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تودّ أن نتبادل بطاقات العمل؟
expressions.example: Would you like to exchange business cards? Yes, that would be great!

expressions.meaning_en: Thank someone for asking you to come.
expressions.example: Thank you for inviting me to the meeting.

grammar.title: "How are you?" vs "How have you been?"
grammar.explanation_ar: How are you? نسأل بها عن الحال الآن. How have you been? نسأل بها صديقًا لم نره منذ مدة، عن الفترة الماضية حتى الآن، والجواب: I've been good. (المضارع التام: have/has + التصريف الثالث)
grammar.explanation_en: "How are you?" asks about now. "How have you been?" asks about the time since you last met (present perfect: have + past participle).
examples: How are you? I am fine, thank you.
How have you been? I've been good, thanks!
I haven't seen them in a while.

grammar.title: Polite forms: would like / I'll have / May I ask
grammar.explanation_ar: في الكلام الرسمي والمهذب نستخدم: Would you like...? (هل تودّ) و I would like that (أودّ ذلك) و May I ask...? (هل لي أن أسأل) و I'll have... لطلب الطعام.
grammar.explanation_en: Polite forms: Would you like...? / I would like... / May I ask...? / I'll have... (ordering).
examples: Would you like to exchange business cards?
May I ask, what is your role in your company?
I will have a mocha, please.

grammar.title: Present simple: talking about yourself
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم المضارع البسيط للحقائق والعادات: I come here every week. I like to read. ومع he/she نضيف s: He focuses on clients. She likes to play.
grammar.explanation_en: Use the present simple for facts and habits. Add -s with he/she.
examples: She likes to play in the park.

questions.question: Which greeting is formal?
questions.explanation_ar: Good afternoon, Mr Smith تحية رسمية.

questions.question: It is a pleasure to meet you. — ___
questions.explanation_ar: الرد الرسمي: The pleasure is mine.
questions.explanation_en: The formal reply is "The pleasure is mine".

questions.question: How have you been? — I've ___ good, thanks!
questions.explanation_ar: I've been هي اختصار I have been (المضارع التام).

questions.question: What can I get for you today? — I'll ___ a latte, please.
questions.explanation_ar: I'll have... لطلب مشروب أو طعام.

questions.question: A small card with your name and phone number is a ___.
What is an "agenda"?
choices: a list of things to talk about in a meeting
questions.explanation_en: An agenda is a list of meeting topics.

questions.question: We use "Ms" before the name of...
questions.explanation_en: Ms is used for a woman.

questions.question: I look forward ___ your message.
questions.explanation_ar: نقول look forward to بمعنى أتطلّع إلى.

questions.question: Choose the polite question.
choices: May I ask, what is your role in your company?

questions.question: My cat is very ___. She likes to play.
